accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes a tide?
o: An irregular rise of sea level caused by storm winds
A permanent increase in sea level caused by melting ice
A circular movement of ocean water caused by the Coriolis force
A periodic rise and fall of sea level occurring once or twice a day
accepted.x: A tide is the periodic rise and fall of sea level, generally occurring once or twice a day. Storm surges are irregular and weather-driven phenomena.
accepted.tq: Use the precise definition and distinguish tides from storm surges.
accepted.sec: Tides - causes, direct/indirect, spring vs neap, tidal range sites  [other exams]

accepted.s:
With reference to the causes of tides, consider the following statements:
1. The gravitational pull of the Moon is greater than that of the Sun in producing tides.
2. Centrifugal force acts in opposition to gravitational attraction.
3. The vertical component of tide-generating force is more important than the horizontal component.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Moon has the greater tidal influence, and centrifugal force counters gravitational attraction. The horizontal components of the tide-generating force are more significant than the vertical component, making statement 3 false.
accepted.tq: Identify the incorrect comparison of horizontal and vertical components.
accepted.sec: Tides - causes, direct/indirect, spring vs neap, tidal range sites  [other exams]

accepted.s: The tidal bulge on the side of the Earth facing the Moon is primarily produced by
o: the indirect effect of centrifugal force
the direct gravitational attraction of the Moon
accepted.x: The bulge on the side facing the Moon is the direct tide, produced mainly by lunar gravitational attraction.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between direct and indirect tidal bulges.
accepted.sec: Tides - causes, direct/indirect, spring vs neap, tidal range sites  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The tidal bulge on the side opposite to the Moon is associated with centrifugal force.
2. The bulge facing the Moon is called the indirect tide.
3. Two tidal bulges are formed on opposite sides of the Earth.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The opposite-side bulge is associated with centrifugal force and the two bulges occur on opposite sides. The bulge facing the Moon is the direct tide, not the indirect tide.
accepted.tq: Spot the swapped meaning in a confusable pair.
accepted.sec: Tides - causes, direct/indirect, spring vs neap, tidal range sites  [other exams]

accepted.s: The tide-generating force is best represented by the
o: sum of wind force and atmospheric pressure
difference between gravitational attraction and centrifugal force
sum of vertical and horizontal components of wind
difference between ocean temperature and salinity
accepted.x: Tide-generating force results from the difference between gravitational attraction and centrifugal force.
accepted.tq: Test the exact relationship in a definition.
accepted.sec: Tides - causes, direct/indirect, spring vs neap, tidal range sites  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following conditions generally produces higher tidal bulges?
o: A region completely enclosed by sea ice
A narrow mid-ocean island with steep submarine slopes
accepted.x: Tidal bulges are higher over wide continental shelves, whereas they are lower around mid-ocean islands.
accepted.tq: Apply the shelf-versus-island comparison to a physical setting.
accepted.sec: Tides - causes, direct/indirect, spring vs neap, tidal range sites  [other exams]

accepted.s: When tidal water is funnelled into bays, estuaries and channels, it may develop into
accepted.x: The concentration and channelling of tidal water in bays, estuaries and channels produces tidal currents.
accepted.tq: Match a physical process with its direct result.
accepted.sec: Tides - causes, direct/indirect, spring vs neap, tidal range sites  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a characteristic of a storm surge?
o: It is different from an ordinary tide.
It is caused by winds and pressure changes.
It is a periodic astronomical rise and fall of sea level.
accepted.x: A storm surge is an irregular, weather-driven rise of sea level caused by winds and pressure changes. Periodic astronomical movement is a characteristic of tides, not storm surges.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that describes tides rather than storm surges.
accepted.sec: Tides - causes, direct/indirect, spring vs neap, tidal range sites  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a semi-diurnal tide?
o: Two high tides and two low tides in a day
One high tide and one low tide in a day
The lowest tidal range occurring at right angles
Tides of unequal height only during a full moon
accepted.x: A semi-diurnal tide has two high tides and two low tides in a day and is the most common tidal pattern.
accepted.tq: Use the frequency classification of tides.
accepted.sec: Tides - causes, direct/indirect, spring vs neap, tidal range sites  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Type of tide)
A. Semi-diurnal
B. Diurnal
C. Mixed
D. Spring

List-II (Characteristic)
1. One high tide and one low tide a day
2. Tides of unequal height
3. Two high tides and two low tides a day
4. Highest tidal range

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: Semi-diurnal tides have two highs and two lows; diurnal tides have one high and one low; mixed tides are unequal in height; spring tides have the highest range.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure frequency pair and eliminate the remaining codes.
accepted.sec: Tides - causes, direct/indirect, spring vs neap, tidal range sites  [other exams]

accepted.s: The interval between successive high tides is approximately
accepted.x: High tides recur at approximately 12 hours and 25 minutes. The lunar influence makes the interval longer than 12 hours.
accepted.tq: Recall the distinctive numerical interval rather than the rounded solar day.
accepted.sec: Tides - causes, direct/indirect, spring vs neap, tidal range sites  [other exams]

accepted.s: Perigean tides are unusually high because the Moon is
o: at right angles to the Sun
accepted.x: Perigean tides occur when the Moon is closest to the Earth, thereby increasing its gravitational tidal influence.
accepted.tq: Link the astronomical term with its distance condition.
accepted.sec: Tides - causes, direct/indirect, spring vs neap, tidal range sites  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following tidal situations in descending order of tidal range:
A. Neap tide
B. Spring tide
C. Ordinary tide
D. Tidal situation at perigee
accepted.x: Perigean tides are unusually high, followed by spring tides; ordinary tides have an intermediate range and neap tides have the lowest range among the listed conditions.
accepted.tq: Compare the relative range first, then place the lowest-range condition last.
accepted.sec: Tides - causes, direct/indirect, spring vs neap, tidal range sites  [other exams]

accepted.s: At which of the following Indian locations is a tidal range of about 5–10 metres found, along with significant tidal-energy potential?
accepted.x: The Gulf of Khambhat has a tidal range of about 5–10 metres and an estimated tidal-energy potential of approximately 7,000 MW.
accepted.tq: Distinguish closely related Indian tidal-energy sites using the range figure.
accepted.sec: Tides - causes, direct/indirect, spring vs neap, tidal range sites  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Gulf of Khambhat — 5–8 m tidal range
Gulf of Kutch — 5–8 m tidal range
Bay of Fundy — approximately 5 m tidal range
accepted.x: The Gulf of Kutch has a tidal range of about 5–8 metres. The Gulf of Khambhat has about 5–10 metres, the Sundarbans about 5 metres, and the Bay of Fundy has the world's greatest tidal range.
accepted.tq: Compare similar tidal-range figures and reject swapped locations.
accepted.sec: Tides - causes, direct/indirect, spring vs neap, tidal range sites  [other exams]

accepted.s: The world's greatest tidal range is associated with the
accepted.x: The Bay of Fundy in Canada is known for the world's greatest tidal range.
accepted.tq: Test the superlative location directly while using other major sites as distractors.
accepted.sec: Tides - causes, direct/indirect, spring vs neap, tidal range sites  [other exams]

accepted.s: Chandipur on the coast of Odisha is notable because, during low tide,
o: the sea freezes near the coast
the sea level remains permanently high
a warm current meets a cold current
the sea recedes several kilometres from the shoreline
accepted.x: At Chandipur, the sea recedes several kilometres from the shoreline at low tide.
accepted.tq: Use a distinctive place-specific geographical feature.
accepted.sec: Tides - causes, direct/indirect, spring vs neap, tidal range sites  [other exams]

accepted.s: Tidal energy can be harnessed through
o: only wind turbines placed on beaches
barrages across estuaries and underwater turbines
desalination plants located on continental shelves
accepted.x: Tidal energy is harnessed through tidal-range systems, such as barrages across estuaries, and tidal-stream systems using underwater turbines.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the two technological methods from unrelated coastal infrastructure.
accepted.sec: Tides - causes, direct/indirect, spring vs neap, tidal range sites  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about oceanic gyres:
1. They are large circular current systems.
2. They are formed through the combined influence of winds, the Coriolis force and land barriers.
3. They occur only in the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Gyres are large circular systems formed by winds, Coriolis force and land barriers. They occur in all ocean basins, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Reject the restrictive word ‘only’ when the distribution is broader.
accepted.sec: Sargasso Sea and gyres  [other exams]

accepted.s: In which direction do major ocean gyres generally circulate in the Southern Hemisphere?
accepted.x: Major gyres generally flow anticlockwise in the Southern Hemisphere and clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere.
accepted.tq: Apply the hemispheric Coriolis-direction rule.
accepted.sec: Sargasso Sea and gyres  [other exams]

accepted.s: The clockwise circulation of ocean gyres in the Northern Hemisphere is primarily related to the fact that the Coriolis force deflects moving water to the
accepted.x: In the Northern Hemisphere, the Coriolis force deflects moving water to the right, contributing to clockwise gyre circulation.
accepted.tq: Connect hemispheric deflection with the resulting circulation.
accepted.sec: Sargasso Sea and gyres  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following forms the northern boundary of the Sargasso Sea?
accepted.x: The Sargasso Sea is bounded by the North Atlantic Drift in the north, the Gulf Stream in the west, the Canary Current in the east and the North Equatorial Current in the south.
accepted.tq: Test one boundary of a current-defined region.
accepted.sec: Sargasso Sea and gyres  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly gives the western and eastern boundaries of the Sargasso Sea, respectively?
o: North Equatorial Current and North Atlantic Drift
North Atlantic Drift and North Equatorial Current
accepted.x: The Gulf Stream bounds the Sargasso Sea on the west, while the Canary Current bounds it on the east.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the four surrounding currents by direction.
accepted.sec: Sargasso Sea and gyres  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Sargasso Sea is unusual because it is
o: the only sea bounded by ocean currents rather than land
a sea enclosed entirely by coral reefs
the only sea located in the Southern Hemisphere
accepted.x: The Sargasso Sea lies in the North Atlantic and is bounded by currents rather than land. It is also calm, warm, salty and rich in floating Sargassum weed.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive geographical exception in the definition.
accepted.sec: Sargasso Sea and gyres  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following combinations is correctly matched with the effect of ocean currents?
o: Gulf Stream and Labrador Current — Grand Banks fishing grounds
Kuroshio and Benguela — Grand Banks fishing grounds
Humboldt and California — North Atlantic fog
North Atlantic Drift and Oyashio — Atacama Desert
accepted.x: The warm Gulf Stream and cold Labrador Current meet near the Grand Banks off Newfoundland, creating rich fishing grounds and fog.
accepted.tq: Match a current pair with its well-known regional effect.
accepted.sec: Effects of currents - climate, fishing grounds, fog  [other exams]

accepted.s: The rich fishing grounds off Japan are associated with the meeting of the
accepted.x: The warm Kuroshio Current and cold Oyashio Current meet off Japan, producing favourable fishing conditions.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Japanese current pair from the North Atlantic pair.
accepted.sec: Effects of currents - climate, fishing grounds, fog  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): Fog is frequently formed near Newfoundland.
Reason (R): Warm and cold ocean currents meet in the waters near Newfoundland.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Fog commonly forms where warm and cold currents meet. Near Newfoundland, the Gulf Stream meets the Labrador Current, making the reason the correct explanation.
accepted.tq: Check whether the stated current interaction directly explains the regional phenomenon.
accepted.sec: Effects of currents - climate, fishing grounds, fog  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following cold currents is associated with the Atacama Desert?
accepted.x: The cold Humboldt Current contributes to the arid conditions along the west coast of South America, including the Atacama Desert.
accepted.tq: Match the coastal desert with its associated cold current.
accepted.sec: Effects of currents - climate, fishing grounds, fog  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Desert region)
A. Atacama
B. Namib and Kalahari
C. Sonoran
D. Peru fishery

List-II (Associated current or process)
1. California Current
2. Upwelling associated with the Humboldt Current
3. Humboldt Current
4. Benguela Current

accepted.s: Upwelling of cold, nutrient-rich water is particularly important for fisheries in
o: the central areas of all deserts
Norway and the United Kingdom only
accepted.x: Cold, nutrient-rich upwelling supports fisheries along Peru and near Somalia, where the Somalia or Findlater current system is involved.
accepted.tq: Identify the resource-producing effect of coastal upwelling.
accepted.sec: Effects of currents - climate, fishing grounds, fog  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about ocean currents and climate is correct?
o: Warm currents invariably create deserts on adjacent coasts.
Cold currents along western coasts generally make adjacent coastal lands cooler and drier.
Cold currents always produce humid tropical climates.
Ocean currents have no role in the distribution of global temperature.
accepted.x: Cold currents can cool and dry adjacent western coastal lands, contributing to deserts such as the Atacama and Namib. Ocean circulation also influences global temperature distribution.
accepted.tq: Choose the carefully worded generalisation and reject absolute claims.
accepted.sec: Effects of currents - climate, fishing grounds, fog  [other exams]

accepted.s: The mild climate of north-western Europe and the ice-free condition of ports such as those in Norway and Murmansk are associated with the
accepted.x: The North Atlantic Drift, an extension of the Gulf Stream, carries warm water towards north-western Europe and helps keep its coasts mild and ports ice-free in winter.
accepted.tq: Match a climatic effect and location with the responsible warm current.
accepted.sec: Effects of currents - climate, fishing grounds, fog  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Fishing grounds are often found where warm and cold currents meet.
2. Plankton flourishing in such zones supports marine fisheries.
3. Disruption of ocean circulation can alter global temperature distribution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Current convergence promotes plankton-rich fishing grounds, while changes in circulation can affect the global distribution of temperature.
accepted.tq: Recognise a linked chain of cause, biological effect and climatic consequence.
accepted.sec: Effects of currents - climate, fishing grounds, fog  [other exams]
